title: Where everyone sits after the move
variant: A plan drawn to scale, with names that appear as you zoom in
prompt: We have the new seating plan in a spreadsheet. Draw it as an actual floor plan so we can see what it looks like before the furniture goes in.
note: The plan shape: nothing is draggable, because the positions are measurements rather than opinions, and a reader who moves a desk here has broken the page's only claim. It is the file that uses semantic zoom for real work -- 72 desk labels and 11 room capacities carry `data-from`, so the fitted view is six zones and a count and the names arrive when you go looking for them. The jump chips are generated from the zones themselves so one cannot outlive what it points at. The three findings are all statements about distance, which is the test of whether a plan earned being drawn: if none of the findings need the geometry, a table of names would have done.
